│   you don’t even really have to search for the memories. ime i can start with “i feel upset about X” and relevant memories will just start bubbling up as long as i take a second to notice and not flinch at them. undigested bits of the past triggering microflashbacks
│   ├── 1450556682677800961 [2021-10-19] @QiaochuYuan 💜 188 🔁 10

1. once upon a time i was at an authentic relating event where some of the women became upset at a man there - let's call him raul - for (affectionately) touching people without asking for explicit verbal consent first. the "worst" thing he did was pat a woman on the leg

===

1505771673890353152 [2022-03-21] @QiaochuYuan 💜 37
the local culture there was big on verbal consent for touch. i, on the other hand, said quite clearly when we discussed this that i loved it when raul touched *me* without asking first; he gave me hugs and stuff and it made me feel really warm and loved in a brotherly way
↓
1505771676528693249 [2022-03-21] @QiaochuYuan 💜 30 🔁 1
the women (not the woman he touched, other women) were not happy about this, they were filled with righteous indignation, at one point it got so bad raul was packing up to leave the event early and he was very sad

then we had one last conversation about it as a group
↓
1505771678428672000 [2022-03-21] @QiaochuYuan 💜 31 🔁 1
raul said he came from a more affectionate culture, and when he patted the woman on the leg she was dealing with difficult feelings (about me, as it happens) and he was trying to offer her support wrt that; he felt sad that this positive intent on his part was being missed
↓
1505771679997300743 [2022-03-21] @QiaochuYuan 💜 26 🔁 1
i don't have clear memories of what happened next but iirc some of the women explained more about sexual harassment and assault etc. and at some point raul settled on "okay, i think i get it, i will ask consent before touching the *women*"

then two men spoke up
↓
1505771681578565634 [2022-03-21] @QiaochuYuan 💜 26 🔁 1
one of them insisted that no, consent wasn't something that was just important when interacting with women, it was important for everyone, including men

i don't remember what raul said in response but basically he didn't understand
↓
1505771683252105216 [2022-03-21] @QiaochuYuan 💜 35 🔁 2
the second man, who will forever be a hero to me for this moment, told a (brief) story about a time he had been nonconsensually touched in a sexual way by a man

raul's face changed. you could see it click for him right there. "oh. oh shit"
↓
1505771685030424580 [2022-03-21] @QiaochuYuan 💜 64
this was the second time we were talking about this as a group, and we needed to talk about it this long in order to actually understand what was happening

raul was not acting out of malice. he *genuinely did not understand*, and what helped him understand was *a story*
↓
1505771686611750913 [2022-03-21] @QiaochuYuan 💜 63 🔁 1
authentic relating people talk about "getting someone's world"; understanding what a person's experience is like, what it's like to be them

an abstract claim about consent didn't help raul get anyone's world here. but a story did. and through watching that we got raul's world
↓
1505771688293593093 [2022-03-21] @QiaochuYuan 💜 45
raul came to understand, at the story level, at least a little bit, what it was like to be a person who cared about consent for touch; and in seeing that understanding dawn on raul we came to understand what it was like to be him not understanding that

rating.reasoning_summary: This strand represents a low-cohesion collection of tweets unified only by the keyword 'cheating' rather than a coherent narrative arc. The core intellectual artifact is Qiaochu Yuan's 2021 observation about abstraction as emotional defense ('people get mad about generalities when they're actually heartbroken about specifics'), which generates genuine engagement and application within rationalist/authentic-relating circles. However, the semantic search has pulled in viral relationship drama tweets (2025) that share zero conceptual connection to Yuan's therapeutic insight. The boundary object exists (Yuan's framework for moving from abstraction to specifics), but most tweets are noise—either unrelated viral content or simple quote-retweets without elaboration.

essential_tweets.annotation: The Seed: Yuan's core observation linking heartbreak over specifics to rage about generalities
Methodological turn: Asking people to go 'down levels of abstraction' to specific memories
Key mechanism: Abstraction as emotional defense that shields from painful specifics
The therapeutic loop: Touching specifics, then re-ascending to re-grounded abstractions
Application: PUA guy needed to express confusion/betrayal, not adopt ideology
Meta-moment: Yuan realizes he wrote the thread as self-advice
Story as understanding: Raul's consent epiphany came from a specific narrative, not abstract principle
Yuan self-quotes to critique discourse lacking concrete details
Tasshin's endorsement: The tweet 'lives rent-free' as memorable wisdom
2025 callback: Yuan uses his own tweet to critique antinatalism as symptom of unhappiness
